headline: Anthropic launches Cyber Mission to defend critical systems
dek: The initiative pairs Claude and on-site engineers with infrastructure defenders, per Anthropic and Tecmundo.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Defense for grids and open source
body: Anthropic launched Cyber Mission on Thursday, a long-term initiative to apply AI to defending systems society depends on (Anthropic, Tecmundo).
It starts on two fronts: protecting critical infrastructure such as power grids and water systems, and triaging vulnerabilities in open-source software (Anthropic, Tecmundo).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Two programs, one goal
s3.body: Both fronts put Anthropic's models in defenders' hands (Anthropic).

points.t: Claude, on-site engineers and threat research go to firms that decide which fixes are safe for systems that cannot go offline (Anthropic).
Eleven founding partners, including Accenture, CrowdStrike, Dragos, Hitachi and Rockwell Automation, split by consulting, security and equipment (Anthropic).
A free, opt-in service sends enrolled open-source projects periodic scans, each with an exploit demonstration and a suggested fix (Anthropic).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Defenders are still behind
body: Anthropic and Tecmundo describe the same backdrop: the most advanced defensive tools have not reached enough defenders, while attackers use AI as a weapon (Anthropic, Tecmundo).
OSS Scanner reports are model-generated and sent without human review. That speeds delivery but can bring errors, such as a wrong severity rating (Anthropic).

items.t: The group of providers may grow as strategies prove effective (Anthropic, Tecmundo).
Anthropic says it will work to improve the true-positive rate over time (Anthropic).
Anthropic expects the gains to put defense ahead of AI-enabled attacks; this is its expectation, not an observed result (Tecmundo).

caption.hook: Anthropic launched Cyber Mission, an initiative using AI to defend critical infrastructure, per Anthropic and Tecmundo.
body: Cyber Mission grows out of Project Glasswing, an earlier vulnerability-scanning program. Anthropic says it merged Glasswing that same week into an expanded Cyber Verification Program, which gives more defenders access to its most capable models.

Since June, Anthropic says it has offered Claude models to US state, local and tribal governments, now covering more than half of US states. For outside projects, it will keep sharing only human-verified disclosures (Anthropic).
caption.cta: Which would matter more for defenders, scanning open-source code or fixing industrial systems that cannot go offline?
